correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2,r>=2 and real 0<lambda<=1, the finite-cycle Fourier antipodal energy inequality bounds cross-fiber antipodal distances for any Hilbert embedding, yielding the exact lower bound. An orthogonal regular-polygon/simplex embedding has explicit pairwise squared distances. Separate proved inequalities for within-fiber, same-index, cross separation one, and cross separation k>=2 verify all pairs. The sine lemma is proved by concavity and checked endpoint estimates. The critical Fourier and algebraic factors are independently replayed through 39,342 finite inequalities and 42 conditional-negative-type linear programs; those samples do not substitute for the general proof. Scope and lambda endpoint explicit.

value.rationale: Determines sharp least-distortion Euclidean embeddings for every weighted cycle-of-cliques across infinitely many cycle sizes, fiber cardinalities, and a full continuous edge-weight interval. Exact optimizers and a universal two-fiber obstruction explain unexpected independence from the clique cardinality; the deformation law and monotonicity quantify finite-dimensional metric geometry, not an arbitrary small table. The unweighted boundary is not counted as a new theorem.
